publications.title: 3D Lidar-Based Object Conditions in Adverse Weather Conditions
publications.subtitle: National High School Journal of Science
publications.description: This research focuses on the critical task of lidar-based 3D object detection for autonomous driving, specifically evaluating the performance of convolutional neural networks under adverse weather conditions. The paper examines two leading models, PointPillar and SECOND, both trained on the KITTI dataset in clear weather. Initially, these models achieved average precision values of 51.86% and 70.02%, respectively, under standard conditions. However, when tested on the Canadian Adverse Driving Dataset (CADC) with snowfall, their precision dropped to nearly 0%, highlighting the challenge of object detection in real-world weather conditions. Retraining the models on CADC improved their precision to 48.43% and 49.51%, but resulted in a 0% precision on the KITTI dataset. This study stresses the importance of retraining models for specific environmental conditions to ensure reliable performance in autonomous driving applications.
